metadata.title: Week of Nov 17.
metadata.description: A weekly-progress ai-explainer for Sanjana (@HumanitariansAI): the week of Nov 17 video-QA work as stats only, no names — 48 videos reviewed across 7 creators and 2 projects, a clean sweep (every video cleared the 4K + watermark checks, zero sent back), 22 hours, and the week's milestone: a meeting to scope the next automation stage, automatic YouTube upload triggered after the 4K check. Narrated by Liam (Kokoro am_onyx). Watermarked @HumanitariansAI.

beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Liam for Sanjana, and this is the progress report for the week of November seventeenth. Forty-eight videos reviewed, every one cleared — and the next stage of the automation got mapped out.

props.command: claude "summarize my week — the reviews and the auto-upload plan"

qc.sparse_reason: Headline stat card: four big numbers on cream, a focused glance display like a title card; whitespace is intentional. Edge-bleed and contrast still enforced.

beats.narration_text: The week at a glance. Twenty-two hours of work. Forty-eight videos reviewed and sent for professor approval, across seven creators and two projects. And a clean sweep — every single video passed the checks.

props.title: THE WEEK AT A GLANCE
props.caption: A clean sweep — every video cleared.

beats.role_note: WeekBoard flags — the automation planning meeting (next stage: auto-upload)

qc.sparse_reason: What's-new callout: a short focused flag list on cream; whitespace is intentional like a title card. Edge-bleed and contrast still enforced.

beats.narration_text: What's new this week is the plan. With the four-K auto-check already running, I sat down to scope the next stage: automatic upload to YouTube, triggered once a video clears the four-K check. We walked through how a passing video would hand straight to the upload queue — the review gate feeding the publish step, with no manual copy in between.

props.title: WHAT'S NEW THIS WEEK

props.caption: After the 4K check: automate the upload.

beats.role_note: WeekBoard bars — where the 22 hours went
beats.narration_text: Where the twenty-two hours went. Nine on reviewing videos through to approval. Six on uploads and the quality checks — four-K and watermark. Four on the meeting and write-up for the auto-upload pipeline. And three on the progress sheet and coordination with the creators.

qc.sparse_reason: Review-outcomes chart: a focused two-bar display (48 cleared, 0 sent back) on cream; the clean-week zero bar leaves intentional whitespace. Edge-bleed and contrast still enforced.

beats.narration_text: The outcomes were clean. All forty-eight videos cleared and went on for professor approval. None were sent back — the first week with nothing bounced, which is what the automated four-K gate was supposed to buy us.

So the exceptions list is short, by design. Every video passed the four-K check. Every video carried the watermark. Zero sent back. Code-on-GitHub tracked per project, as always. The gate did its job quietly.

props.title: QUALITY — A CLEAN WEEK
props.caption: The gate did its job quietly.

qc.sparse_reason: Clean-week callout: a short focused flag list on cream (all passed / zero sent back); whitespace is intentional like a title card. Edge-bleed and contrast still enforced.

beats.role_note: composer — next week follows the automation
beats.narration_text: Next week follows the automation one step further. Turn the auto-upload plan into a first working version: when a video passes the four-K check, queue it for YouTube — and keep professor review as the gate before anything goes public.
